about: Zero is an exception, never a pass. These cases are the door's half of that
rule — `evaluation::check` in Rust, `checkEvaluation` in TypeScript. Both must
agree on every one, in both directions.
The motivating measurement: AUTH-24 (`sponsor:edit never implies deploy`),
grounded on the deployer role, examines 0 records in Studio. A check there
would report success forever, having examined nothing. Case
A machine reports, never judges (RFC-004a §4): a case whose `author` carries
`machine_author_prefix` may record Examined / Vacuous / CannotBeGrounded and
is refused a Passes or a Fails — the `judgments`. `Examined` is deliberately
not a judgment: it is the one outcome a machine exists to report.

cases.name: a_pass_over_zero_records_is_refused
cases.why: An invariant that examined nothing succeeds trivially. This is the AUTH-24 finding.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: examined_over_zero_records_is_the_same_lie_in_a_quieter_voice
cases.why: Examined's whole content is 'there were records to look at'. Over zero there were not.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: fails_over_zero_records_is_refused_too
cases.why: A failure over an empty population is as meaningless as a pass over one.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: the_same_zero_honestly_labelled_is_accepted
cases.why: au:Vacuous is the honest recording of 'it ran and examined nothing'. Refusing it would leave nowhere to put the truth.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: a_check_that_could_not_run_at_all_is_accepted
cases.why: au:CannotBeGrounded is 'it could not run', which legitimately carries zero.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: a_real_result_over_real_records_is_accepted
cases.why: The other direction. A refusal only ever shown to refuse is not a check either.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: a_result_with_no_population_at_all_is_refused
cases.why: A missing count is not a zero count — it is a result nobody can audit, and it slips past the zero check precisely because there is nothing to compare.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: a_failure_with_no_population_at_all_is_refused
cases.why: Same hole, the other positive outcome.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: cannot_be_grounded_may_legitimately_have_no_count
cases.why: Nothing ran, so there is nothing to have counted. Demanding a number here would invent a measurement.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: an_unattributed_measurement_is_refused
cases.why: The same claim can pass in one product and be ungroundable in another, and an unattributed count cannot tell you which.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: an_evaluation_of_nothing_is_refused
cases.why: `claim` is required — an evaluation of nothing is not a measurement.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: an_unknown_outcome_is_refused
cases.why: The vocabulary is closed. There is deliberately no Unknown bucket — it would immediately become where anything awkward went.
cases.author: a@b.c

cases.name: a_machine_may_report_what_it_examined
cases.why: RFC-004a §4: a consumer's CI posts a count under a machine principal. A count over real records is a measurement, and Examined is exactly 'measured, undecided'.
cases.author: machine:studio-nextjs

cases.name: a_machine_may_not_judge_a_pass
cases.why: A count says how many records a check would examine. Whether the claim holds over them is a judgment, and a SELECT count(*) did not make one. A machine reports, never judges.
cases.author: machine:studio-nextjs

cases.name: a_machine_zero_honestly_labeled_is_accepted
cases.why: The job that finds nothing says Vacuous, and the door takes it from a machine exactly as it does from a person.
cases.author: machine:studio-nextjs

cases.name: a_machine_examined_over_zero_is_still_refused
cases.why: The machine rule ADDS a refusal and removes none: Examined over zero is the same lie whoever tells it.
cases.author: machine:studio-nextjs
